---
title: "Types and Sample Spaces"
---

A set can hold anything.
It can hold symbols, numbers, stories, or worlds.

So before we talk about outcomes,
we must answer a deeper question:

What *kind* of things* are our outcomes?

This is the question of **type**.

---

### 🔰 Type is structure

A type is not decoration.
It is meaning.

A Boolean type has equality, but not magnitude.

A category type has labels, but not a ruler.

An ordinal type has an order, but no consistent notion of distance.

A number type lives inside an algebraic world:
we can add, scale, invert, compare.

Change the type, and you change what is lawful.
You change what statements even make sense.

And you change what models are allowed.

---

### 💡 Types are alphabets

If reality is a signal, a type is the alphabet.

A dice roll has an alphabet of six symbols.

A day of the week has an alphabet of seven symbols.

A real measurement has an alphabet so dense we treat it as continuous.

We are not just counting possibilities.
We are choosing an alphabet with rules.

Those rules are where probability learns to live.

---

### ⚙️ Type precedes probability

A probability measure does not fall out of the sky.
It is defined on **events**.

Events are subsets of the sample space.

But “subset” is only meaningful once the members of Ω are typed,
so we can sensibly compare, group, and reason about them.

So the order is:

type first,
then outcomes and events,
then probability.

---

### 🪄 Parameters become possible later

We will later talk about **parameters**.

Parameters are not outcomes.
They are coordinates inside a family of distributions.

But you can’t even define such a family
until the outcomes are typed.

Type chooses what shapes are possible.
Type chooses what geometry “shape” even has.

Parameters are the knobs on a machine,
but the type is the blueprint that tells you what machine you built.

---

### ☯ A closing thought

We often think data is numbers.

But data is not a number.
Data is an agreement about *what counts as* a number,
and what counts as a category,
and what counts as a signal.

That agreement is type.

Only then do outcomes become outcomes,
and events become events,
and randomness can be discussed with clarity.
